# 0030. Code generation and packaging: details the specification leaves open

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-04
- Blueprint origin: §5.3 (build output, reproducibility), §2.2 (logic as JavaScript, data as JSON); `spec/runtime-abi.md` §2–§6; `spec/compiler-architecture.md` §4.10–§4.12, §5, §6; `spec/gpu-layout.md` §5, §7; `spec/scenes.md` §11; `spec/testing.md` §3.1, §4.1, §4.3, §7; `spec/tooling.md` §2–§4; decisions 0011, 0013, 0018, 0019, 0028, 0029.

## Context

Task M1-17 turns a checked M1 program into the `dist/` of `spec/runtime-abi.md` §2: `app.js`, its source map, `app.d.ts`, `runtime.d.ts`, the hashed runtime bundle, `program.manifest.json`, the shaders with their span maps and `index.html`, plus the library `build` entry point and replace-on-success writing. The specification fixes the export surface, the manifest schema, the file names and the reproducibility requirement; it does not fix the shape of `BuildResult`, where the code lives, the generated names and statement order of `init`, the order of manifest arrays and spans, how numbers are printed, the canonical form hashed into the build id, what happens when a user module sits where the embedded prelude lives, or how the codegen goldens are organised. They are fixed here so that they are visible, testable and changeable by a later record.

## Decision

All of the following are **proposals** (design choices), not external constraints.

1. **Public API.** `build(&ProjectRoot, &dyn Fs, &CompileOptions) -> BuildResult { project_name, sources, report, files, build_id, out_dir }`. `files` is the whole `dist/` tree as `BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>` keyed by `/`-separated paths, empty when the report has an error; `build_id` and `out_dir` (`build.out_dir`) are what the CLI needs for replace-on-success; `sources` is the build's source map (the project's sources plus the prelude modules the build used), so diagnostics pointing into the prelude render. `CompileOptions { profile, mode, runtime_bundle, runtime_declarations }` as in §4.12; `CompileOptions::with_stub_runtime(mode)` uses `STUB_RUNTIME_BUNDLE` (`// mtek test runtime stub\n`) and `STUB_RUNTIME_DECLARATIONS` (`// mtek test runtime declarations stub\n`). A missing bundle **or** missing declarations is `E9030` (one diagnostic naming what is missing); the front end still runs, so the program's own errors are reported too. `BuildMode::Preview` (M6) is `E9010`. A program with errors gets exactly `check`'s diagnostics and no files.
2. **Modules.** `emit_js/ast.rs` (JS AST and printer), `emit_js/program.rs` (`emit_program(program, plan, parts) -> JsModule`), `emit_js/source_map.rs` (VLQ writer, Source Map v3), `emit_js/dts.rs` (`app.d.ts`); `plan/mod.rs` (resource plan); `package/manifest.rs` (serde model), `package/spans.rs` (span table), `package/builder.rs` (`package`), `package/identity.rs` (hashes, build id), `package/html.rs`, `package/replace.rs` (replace-on-success plan); `build.rs` at the crate root. `plan` and `package` are covered by the determinism guard.
3. **`app.js`.** First line `// Generated by mtek <compiler> for language <language>. Do not edit.` (ASCII: all generated code is ASCII, so source-map columns are bytes). Then `export { mountMtek } from "./runtime.<h16>.js";`, `abi`, `baseUrl`, `manifestUrl`, the module-private writer functions of `builtin:frame`, `builtin:object` and every material block (by layout id) exactly as M0-05 emits them, `writers`, `functions` (`{}`), the scene initialiser `function s_<Name>_init(ctx)` (`s_` is never produced by user-name mangling), `scenes` with the **entry scene only**, `prefabs` (`{}`), `export default { abi, baseUrl, manifestUrl, writers, functions, scenes, prefabs };` and `//# sourceMappingURL=app.js.map`. **No `import * as rt` line** until generated code calls an `rt` helper (M2): M1 code needs none, and the runtime bundle exports none yet. The scene entry is `{ init, update: null, fixedUpdate: null, entityUpdate: [null × entities], entityFixedUpdate: [null × entities], events: {}, bindings: [] }` — the shapes of the runtime's `MtekProgramScene` (arrays and objects where the type requires them, `null` inside them for what is not supported). Values use the CPU representation of §4.1 as plain object literals (`{ x, y, z }`, `{ r, g, b, a }`, `{ x, y, z, w }`), `mat4` as `new Float32Array([…])`; `f32` literals are the shortest text that reads back as the binary32 value when read as a JavaScript number (`0.10000000149011612`).
4. **`init(ctx)`.** The active camera and the entities in declaration order (entities in stable instance order); only the active camera, as v0.1 has no camera switching and `ctx.setCamera` addresses the active one. Camera: `setCamera("position")`, then `"target"` if declared else `"rotation"`, then `"projection.fov_y"` or `"projection.height"`, `"projection.near"`, `"projection.far"`. Entity: `const e<i> = ctx.e[<i>];`, `setTransform` for `position`, `rotation`, `scale`, `setVisible`, then `setParam` for every material parameter in declaration order. **Every value is set, defaults included** (the runtime pre-creates records with zero values; a zero scale is invalid). In M1 every value is a constant, so the order of fields inside an entity is not observable and is registry order; M3, which adds initialisers that read state or call `cpu` functions, must follow declaration order. No span ids are passed (the ABI-1 setters take none).
5. **Manifest.** Key order is the order of the schema's `properties` (the model in `package/manifest.rs`; a discriminator that the schema places later is a flattened tagged enum). Numbers are kept as written (`Num`); the compiler writes an `f32` as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same binary32 value (`0.1`, so `Math.fround` recovers it exactly). A layout's root struct node has no `name` (the schema's rule); nested struct nodes keep theirs. Arrays: `layouts` = `builtin:frame`, `builtin:object`, then material blocks by id (`builtin:light` is a nested helper and not listed); `materials` and `shaders` by material symbol; `meshes` one per distinct descriptor (compared bit for bit) in first-use order of the instance order, ids `mesh:<n>`; `materialInstances` one per entity with a material, in entity order, every param `initial`, `shareable: true`; `symbols` = scene, cameras, entities, then per material its declaration (`material`) and params (`param`). `spans` are interned in first-request order: symbols, material params, shader span maps. Material param types come from the instance (the IR), their spans are the `param` declarations in the prelude. `ambientColor`, `ambientIntensity` and `gravity` are the registry defaults of the `Scene` schema until M4/M5; `requiredCapabilities` is empty (profile `webgpu-core-2026` is the default limits); `subsystems.physics` is `false`.
6. **Build identity.** `buildId = sha256` of compact JSON with keys in lexicographic order: `assets` (`[path, sha256]` pairs sorted, none before M4), `compilerVersion`, `config` (the `mtek.toml` text as stored), `features` (`requiredCapabilities.features`, sorted: the "enabled features" of §5.3), `languageVersion`, `runtimeAbi`, `sources` (`[path, sha256]` of every source of the build, prelude included, sorted by path), `targetProfile`. The build mode and the runtime bundle are not part of it: the same program has the same id in every mode (only `index.html` differs by mode).
7. **The prelude.** `std/materials.mtek` is added to the build's source map, after the project's sources, only when a built-in material is used (always, in M1, when an entity has a mesh). A project module there would give the manifest two sources with one path and make `std/materials.mtek::Unlit` ambiguous, so **`project.entry` inside the top-level `std/` directory is `E9001`** ("must be a path outside the directory 'std/', which is reserved for the embedded standard library"); this amends decision 0018 item 2. M2 imports must reject `std/` paths the same way (with the import diagnostics of that task).
8. **Other files.** `program.manifest.json` and `shaders/<h16>.mtek-map.json` are pretty JSON (two-space indentation) with a final line break. `app.js.map` is compact JSON `{ version: 3, file: "app.js", sources, names: [], mappings }` with a final line break; `sources` are the project-relative paths of the referenced `.mtek` files (no `sourcesContent`: no source text is shipped, decision 0019), and M1 maps the start of every statement of `init` (column = its indentation) to its Mtek span; M2-07 maps expressions. `app.d.ts` declares `export interface Inputs {}` until M3. `runtime.d.ts` is the caller's bytes verbatim.
9. **`index.html`.** `release`: the bootstrap of §6.5. `test`: `window.__mtekMount = (options) => mountMtek(document.getElementById("mtek"), program, options);` and no automatic mount. `dev`: the release bootstrap plus the reload client — `new EventSource("/__mtek/events")`, reload on `build-succeeded`, `console.error` the diagnostics on `build-failed` (M1 behaviour of `spec/tooling.md` §4). The title is `[build] title` (default: the project name), HTML-escaped.
10. **Replace on success.** `package::replace::ReplacePlan` is a pure plan: remove a stale `<out_dir>.tmp-<id>`, write the file set into it, rename `<out_dir>` to `<out_dir>.old-<id>` if it exists, rename the temporary directory to `<out_dir>`, remove the old one; `recovery(step)` lists what restores the previous output after a failed step (remove the temporary tree; after a failed swap, move the old output back). An `out_dir` without a final directory name (`.`) has no plan. `crates/mtek-cli/src/dist.rs` executes it (`write_dist`); `mtek build` (M1-19) calls it.
11. **Goldens and tests.** The codegen fixtures are `tests/codegen/scene_a_target_camera_box/` and `tests/codegen/scene_b_orthographic_nested/`: `mtek.toml`, `src/main.mtek` byte-identical to the semantic pass scenes of decision 0027 (a test enforces it; fixture A sets a `[build] title` with characters HTML must escape), and `expected/` built in **release** mode with the stub bundle and stub declarations, minus the bundle file. They carry no `exec.json` in M1 (there are no functions). Instead of building with the real bundle (`spec/testing.md` §4.1), the Node execution test `tests/codegen/app.test.ts` imports the golden `app.js` with a stand-in module under the hashed runtime name: M1 code calls no runtime helper, so the bundle's content cannot affect it. When generated code first imports `rt` (M2), that test must build with the real bundle. The hygiene scan of `spec/testing.md` §4.3 ignores comments and string literals and matches whole identifiers.
12. **Shared example.** `tests/abi/manifests/valid/full.json` had the keys of its assets and material instances out of schema order; they are reordered (JSON-semantically identical) so the Rust model round-trips every valid example byte-identically.

## Consequences

- No new dependency (`serde`, `serde_json`, `sha2`, `jsonschema` as a dev-dependency are in decision 0007's table) and no new diagnostic code. `E9030` is now reported by the library and covered by `tests/build.rs`.
- M1-18 (rendering) reads structure from the manifest and every value from `init(ctx)`: it must implement `ctx.e`, `ctx.setCamera`, `ctx.setTransform`, `ctx.setVisible` and `ctx.setParam` (through the material's field writer from `writers`) before the first frame, and accept `entityUpdate`/`entityFixedUpdate` arrays of `null`.
- M1-19 (CLI) calls `build` with the embedded bundle and `runtime.d.ts`, writes `files` with `dist::write_dist(out_dir, build_id, files)` (removing the `expect(dead_code)` on the module), and maps `has_errors()` to exit code 1.
- M1-20 (browser fixtures) builds with `--mode test` and calls `window.__mtekMount(options)`.
- `spec/compiler-architecture.md` §4.10–§4.12 point here.

## Verification

`crates/mtek-compiler/tests/build.rs` (goldens, reproducibility over every codegen and semantic pass fixture in every mode with shuffled listings, schema validity, span line/columns against the source map, content-addressed names, hygiene, no absolute paths, no entity or camera values in the manifest, modes, `E9030`, `E9010`, programs with errors), `tests/manifest_model.rs` (round trip of every valid example, schema failures agree with the runtime's), `src/package/*.rs`, `src/emit_js/*.rs`, `src/plan/mod.rs`, `src/project/parse/tests.rs` and `tests/semantics/fail/e9001_entry_in_reserved_std_directory/` (the reserved directory), `crates/mtek-cli/src/dist.rs` (replace on success on temporary directories, injected failures), `tests/codegen/app.test.ts` (export surface, writers against the independent encoder, `init` calls against the IR golden), `packages/runtime-web/src/abi/abi.test.ts` (the compiled manifests pass `checkManifest`), `packages/runtime-web/src/runtime-dts.test.ts` (a strict host snippet against the compiled `app.d.ts`).
